answer: Uncertain. There may be a meteg on the מ (vowel: segol), but I can't confirm it. There is no meteg on ר (patach) or ח (chataf patach) that I can see.
visible_evidence: The whole word רחמיך and all its lower points are visible. Under ר: a single patach dash, with no vertical stroke next to it. Under ח: a chataf patach (a dash with two dots), and no stroke. Under מ: two upper dots of a segol. Below them, where the segol's single bottom dot should be, is a vertical stroke that runs down past where the vowel row normally ends. This could be a meteg printed straight under the segol. It could also be the segol's bottom dot printed or smeared into a longer mark. It is centered rather than offset to one side, so I can't tell it apart from a vowel stem. There is no separate lower dot alongside the stroke. ך carries a qamatz inside it. There is no ink from neighboring lines touching the word's lower points.
